notes: Page 2 is an informational page (Architecture, Engineering and Construction history text with photos); it has no building steps, so no pieces or joins are added.
The parts list was provided with this first page, but no pieces are placed on this page.
Page 3 is an informational 'Facts at a Glance' page (location, architect, height, points of interest, photo). It has no building steps, so no pieces or joins are added.
Step 1: two black 4x10 plates are placed side by side along their long edges to form an 8x10 base. They only touch edge to edge, so b2 has no piece beneath it; this is recorded as a contact join.

Step 2: four 1x8 tiles, three plain and one printed 'Seattle Space Needle', go on the base edges. The printed tile is on the front edge. From the picture I judged that each tile lies across the seam between the two plates and so rests on both. The exact edge each tile sits on is not clear.
Part types and colours are taken from the parts list. The page art is very dark.
Step 3: two light bluish gray 4x6 plates sit side by side on the black base, one on each 4x10 plate (b1 and b2), between the black end tiles. They meet edge to edge, so I added a contact join.

Step 4: four light bluish gray 1x6 tiles frame the 4x6 plates. The art is dark and the tile layout is hard to read. I assumed b9 sits on b7, b10 on b8, and b11 and b12 across both plates. The exact positions may be wrong.
Pieces b3 to b6 from page 4 are not shown as rests_on targets because these parts sit on the base plates, not on the black tiles.

Step 5: two round 2x2 plates with axle hole are stacked (b13 on b14) in a 2x2 gap among four 2x2 tiles. An Axle 5 (b15) goes through both axle holes and stands up from the base. It is the part marked with a 1:1 length of 5.
I assumed the stack sits on b7 only. The art is dark, so it may sit across the seam between b7 and b8. The tile assignments are also an estimate.

Step 6: one 6x6 inverted dish (b20) goes on top of the round plate stack. The axle passes through its centre. The dish has no axle-hole port in the catalogue, so the axle join uses no port on the dish side.
Step 7: three angled axle-and-pin connectors (b21 to b23) go onto the three axles of a 120-degree hub (b24). The hub is then pushed onto the top of the central Axle 5 (b15) so it lies on the dish.

The hub has no axle-hole port in the catalogue, so the join from b15 to the hub uses no port on the hub side. I set the hub's rests_on to the dish (b20), though it is not clutched by studs. The angled connectors have no stud contact, so their rests_on is empty.
The 1:1 inset shows the legs at 120 degrees with the pin-hole ends pointing outward.

Step 8: a bush (b25) and two 20-tooth bevel gears (b26, b27) are slid down the central Axle 5 (b15) in that order, from the bottom up. The bush sits on the hub (b24). I took the two gears to be lego-32198.

Step 9: four light bluish gray cylinders are stacked on the axle to form the tower shaft. I identified them as lego-59443 axle connectors, since 6 are in the parts list. Four red Axle 2 Notched (lego-32062) are placed one in the top of each connector. Each red axle fits into the connector below and the one above, so the column is continuous with a red tip on top.
The identification of the grey cylinders is uncertain, because the page art is tiny. Stacked connectors have no studs, so the lower piece is used as the rests_on target.

Step 10: one more light bluish gray cylinder, which I took to be lego-59443, goes on the red axle tip (b35) at the top of the column. An Axle 3 (b37, the part marked 3) is pushed into its top. The page shows the 1:1 length of 3.
Step 11: a wedge belt wheel (pulley, lego-4185) goes onto Axle 3 and sits on the top connector (b36).
The wheel's orientation is shown by the dashed lines. It does not change the connections.

Step 12: a bush (b40, the second lego-32123b) is slid onto Axle 3 (b37) above the pulley. A light bluish gray connector (b39, lego-59443) then goes on top. The art shows the bush already on the axle under the arrow, so I took it as placed first.
Step 13: a second Axle 5 (b41, the part marked 5) is pushed into the top of the connector (b39). The page shows the 1:1 length of 5.
Stacked axle parts have no studs, so rests_on gives the piece directly below.

Step 14: three angled axle-and-pin connectors (b42 to b44) are fitted onto the three axles of a second 120-degree hub (b45). The hub is pushed onto Axle 5 (b41) near its top, so it sits on the connector b39.
As on page 7, the hub has no axle-hole port in the catalogue, so the join from b41 to the hub uses no port on the hub side.
Step 14 is built the same way as step 7, but I did not use a repeat because the second sub-assembly goes on a different shaft. The 1:1 inset shows the leg orientation.

Step 15: each of the three rigid hoses (lego-75c20) is cut to 5.25 in / 133 mm (scissors icon). Each bottom end is pushed into the pin hole of one lower angled connector (b21 to b23), and each hose is bent inward to carry the legs up to the upper hub. Hoses have no ports in the catalogue, so joins use no port on the hose.

The page shows only one hose being fitted. The upper end of the first hose is shown in a pin hole of an upper connector (b42 to b44). I assumed each of the three hoses links one lower connector to one upper connector, pairing b21 with b42, b22 with b43 and b23 with b44. The page does not show which pairs go together.
No stud contacts here, so rests_on is empty.

Step 16: a second 6x6 inverted dish (b49) goes over the top of Axle 5 (b41), above the upper hub (b45) and the angled connectors. A round 2x2 plate with axle hole (b50) is pressed onto the dish's central hollow studs, and the axle passes through its axle hole.

The dish has no axle-hole port in the catalogue, so the axle join to the dish uses no port on the dish side. I set the dish's rests_on to the hub (b45), which it sits on, although the hub has no studs to clutch it.
The upper hoses and connectors are not shown to touch the dish.

Step 17: one 40-tooth gear (lego-3649, b51) is slid onto the top of Axle 5 (b41) and rests on the round 2x2 plate (b50) on the dish. The page has no arrow; the gear is shown at the top of the tower, so I assumed it goes on the axle.

Step 18: a third 6x6 inverted dish (b52) is the roof. A third round 2x2 plate with axle hole (b53) is pressed into the underside of the dish, as the arrows show. The pair then goes over the top of Axle 5 (b41), so the plate sits on the 40-tooth gear (b51).
The gear has no studs, so the plate's rests_on is the gear it sits on. The dish's stud-to-underside clutch is recorded as the dish resting on the plate (b53).
The dish has no axle-hole port in the catalogue, so the axle passes through it as a join with no port on the dish side.

Step 19: the pinnacle is built as a sub-assembly and then placed on the roof dish (b52). A round 1x1 plate (b56) is pressed onto the central stud of the 4x4 inverted dish (b55). A 2x2 inverted dish (b57) goes on top of that. The 1x4 antenna (b54) is pushed onto the stud of the 2x2 dish. The whole stack is placed on the hollow studs in the centre of the 6x6 roof dish (b52).
The 2x2 dish and the 4x4 dish have only 'anti' ports and 'stud.1' respectively in the catalogue, so the joins are recorded as resting on the piece below.

The earlier page replies put pieces in `pieces` and `other_joins` fields, which the output schema does not have. That is why the checker saw missing parts. This reply moves all 57 pieces (b1 to b57) into `parts` with a colour prop, and every earlier rests_on and other_joins link into `edges`.
Stud and anti-stud clutches are `joined` edges. Pieces that only sit on something without clutching, such as a hub or gear on an axle, are `contact` edges. The axle joins are `joined` edges.

Hubs, dishes and hoses have no matching port in the catalogue for some joins, so those edges leave the port on that side null. The tile layout on pages 4 and 5 and the hose pairing on page 15 are estimates from the dark page art.
Pages 2, 3 and 17 to 20 have no building steps and add nothing.
